title: Optimizing a reduction, in order
summary: The classic sequence of reduction optimizations, from the naive kernel to a fast one.

items.text: Add two elements during the load from global memory, halving the number of blocks.
Have each thread sum many elements with a grid-stride loop before the block reduction, so a fixed grid covers any `n`.
Make active threads contiguous with `index = 2 * stride * t`: no divergence, but bank conflicts.
Interleaved addressing with `if (t % (2 * stride) == 0)`: correct, but warps diverge.
Sequential addressing (`s[t] += s[t + stride]` for halving strides): no conflicts, but half the threads idle from the first step.
Finish the last 32 values with warp shuffles instead of shared memory and barriers.
